title: Review Solit’s work

reviews.final_reply:
**PASS — the addendum is appropriately bounded.**

The trace distinguishes 2,237 retained training rows from 9,971 current candidates. Its counts are internally consistent; I did not recount the underlying corpora. Missing spelling matches are correctly treated as inconclusive about missing meanings or training exposure.

The next local step—checking nonpanel occurrences, meanings, participant roles, target languages and supervision—is justified. Keep any “learned-task failure” diagnosis conditional: finding a relevant training example does not prove the model learned it.

No required correction. The revised tensor-check and unallocated-time wording is sound. Any adapter-off/on run remains a separate, conditional proposal requiring authorization.

“Berlin” means **BERLIN6, one Pahlavi test passage**. “Severity” means the seriousness of its translation errors. Both reviewers rejected it; one saw a critical error because “3 measures of barley” may have become “day 3.” That interpretation remains disputed.

**Astra review: PASS for the completed experiment’s reporting.** Both methods produced **1 accepted translation out of 3**, with no additional acceptance from self-analysis. Berlin’s disagreement does not change that conclusion.

I verified the 46 recovered files, nine actual prompt/token sequences, analysis dependencies, and scoring arithmetic. The approximately **$0.45** compute estimate checks out; it is not an invoice.

Feedback for Sol: the bounded coverage/exposure investigation is appropriate. Keep dataset presence separate from evidence that the model learned something. Consider an adapter-off/on comparison only if it answers a concrete remaining question; this result authorizes no further paid run.
